facts.sourceExcerpt: Follow the indication-specific order and protocol.
facts.rationale: General order and protocol verification remains a bedside safeguard. The indication-specific distinctions are assessed separately.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Verify syringe strength and the ordered dose.
facts.rationale: Distinguish a full syringe with the exact prescribed strength from an underdose.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Assess for bleeding
facts.rationale: Recognize concealed blood loss even without external bleeding.

facts.sourceExcerpt: check platelets
facts.rationale: Recognize a substantial platelet fall that warrants HIT evaluation.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Severe renal impairment (CrCl below 30 mL/min) requires regimen review because enoxaparin exposure increases.
facts.rationale: Identify the CrCl cutoff that triggers an indication-specific review.

facts.sourceExcerpt: check platelets and renal function as ordered
facts.rationale: Use measured renal function to identify the severe-impairment threshold.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Report the dose and time of the last injection before an invasive procedure or neuraxial catheter placement/removal.
facts.rationale: Identify both last-dose amount and actual administration time as critical procedural information.

facts.sourceExcerpt: New midline back pain, leg weakness or numbness, or bowel/bladder dysfunction after a neuraxial procedure requires immediate escalation for possible spinal hematoma.
facts.rationale: Recognize and immediately escalate possible compressive spinal or epidural bleeding.
